en: To press something so hard that it becomes flat or loses its shape; also a vegetable, or a ball game.
ex: Don't squash the bread at the bottom of the bag.
別把袋子底部的麵包壓扁了。

en: A military operation in which an army surrounds a place to force it to surrender.
ex: The city was under siege for six months.
這座城市被圍困了六個月。

en: Done or chosen without any plan, pattern or purpose.
ex: The winners were chosen at random.
得獎者是隨機抽選出來的。

en: To begin again after a pause; also a short summary of your work history.
ex: Talks will resume next week after the break.
談判將在休會後的下週恢復。

en: Broken pieces left after something has been destroyed.
ex: Rescue workers searched the debris for survivors.
救援人員在瓦礫中搜尋倖存者。

en: One event in a series; or one part of a TV or radio series.
ex: I missed the last episode of the show.
我錯過了那個節目的最後一集。

en: The things that will happen to someone in the future, believed to be controlled by fate.
ex: He believed it was his destiny to become a doctor.
他相信成為醫生是他的命運。

en: A brave and experienced soldier or fighter, especially in the past.
ex: The warrior fought bravely to defend his village.
那位戰士英勇戰鬥以保衛他的村莊。

en: To draw a line under a word; or to show that something is important.
ex: Underline the key words in each sentence.
把每個句子中的關鍵字劃上底線。

en: To sit close to the ground with your knees bent; or to live illegally in an empty building.
ex: The children squatted down to look at the bug.
孩子們蹲下來看那隻蟲。

en: Very attractive or beautiful.
ex: You look gorgeous in that dress.
你穿那件洋裝看起來美極了。

en: A person chosen to represent others at a meeting; or to give part of your work to someone else.
ex: A good manager knows how to delegate tasks.
好的主管懂得如何授權分派任務。

en: The act of watching and directing a person or activity to make sure things are done correctly.
ex: Young children need adult supervision near water.
幼童在水邊需要大人監督。

en: Used after a noun or 'any' or 'no' to emphasize that nothing at all is meant.
ex: There is no evidence whatsoever to support his claim.
完全沒有證據支持他的說法。

en: Favoring new ideas and social reform; or developing step by step.
ex: The city adopted progressive policies on recycling.
這座城市在回收方面採取了進步的政策。

en: To tell someone that something is good or suitable for a purpose.
ex: Can you recommend a good restaurant nearby?
你能推薦附近一家好餐廳嗎？

en: Something that exists as a separate unit, such as a company or organization.
ex: The firm is a separate legal entity from its owners.
這家公司在法律上是獨立於所有人的實體。

en: A firm hold on something; or to hold tightly; also control over a person or situation.
ex: She gripped the rope with both hands.
她雙手緊抓著繩子。

en: A surprising situation in which two similar things happen at the same time by chance.
ex: It was pure coincidence that we met at the airport.
我們在機場遇見純屬巧合。

en: To judge or decide the value, quality or amount of something.
ex: Inspectors came to assess the damage after the storm.
暴風雨後，檢查員前來評估損失。

en: A person who cannot stop drinking alcohol; or containing alcohol.
ex: Beer and wine are alcoholic drinks.
啤酒和葡萄酒是含酒精的飲料。

en: Able to say clever and funny things.
ex: He is known for his witty remarks at parties.
他在派對上以機智的言論聞名。

en: A belief in magic or luck that is not based on reason or science.
ex: It is a superstition that black cats bring bad luck.
黑貓帶來厄運是一種迷信。

en: An organized plan to achieve something; or a secret plan to gain an advantage.
ex: The government introduced a new housing scheme.
政府推出了一項新的住房計畫。

en: A period of time spent on a particular activity; or a formal meeting of a court or parliament.
ex: The class has a two-hour session every Friday.
這門課每週五有兩小時的課程。

en: Deserving respect because of being honest and having high moral standards.
ex: He made an honorable decision to resign.
他做出了光明磊落的辭職決定。

en: A group of people, teams or countries that join together for a common purpose.
ex: Our team won the league championship this year.
我們的球隊今年贏得了聯賽冠軍。

en: A tall upright post that supports a building; or an important supporter of something.
ex: Stone pillars held up the roof of the temple.
石柱撐著寺廟的屋頂。

en: Advice, or a lawyer who gives legal advice; also to advise someone.
ex: The defendant's counsel asked for more time.
被告的律師要求更多時間。

en: To give a disease to someone; or to spread bad feelings or ideas to others.
ex: The virus can infect people of all ages.
這種病毒可以感染各個年齡層的人。

en: A natural ability to do something; or all the teachers in a university or school department.
ex: The faculty voted to change the curriculum.
全體教師投票決定更改課程。

en: The floor at the bottom of a doorway; or the point at which something begins or changes.
ex: The scientist is on the threshold of a major discovery.
那位科學家即將有重大發現。

en: A fixed and oversimplified idea about a type of person or thing.
ex: The film challenges old stereotypes about older people.
這部電影挑戰了對老年人的舊有刻板印象。

en: The row of small bones down the middle of the back; also a sharp point on a plant or animal.
ex: The cold wind sent a shiver down my spine.
寒風讓我背脊發涼。

en: To turn something over quickly, or to throw something lightly into the air.
ex: Let's flip a coin to decide who goes first.
我們擲硬幣來決定誰先開始。

en: A person whose rank is just below the leader, and who acts for the leader when needed.
ex: The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
經理不在時，副手負責主持。

en: A part of a whole; or the correct relationship between the size or amount of two things.
ex: A large proportion of the students come from abroad.
相當大比例的學生來自國外。

en: An action taken in advance to prevent something bad from happening.
ex: Take an umbrella as a precaution against rain.
帶把傘以防下雨。

en: To speak quietly and not clearly, so that others can hardly hear.
ex: He mumbled something and walked out of the room.
他嘟囔了幾句就走出了房間。

en: To protect someone or something from harm or danger; also a flat piece of armor carried on the arm.
ex: She raised her hand to shield her eyes from the sun.
她舉起手遮住眼睛擋太陽。
